newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - New loans and other news.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - New loans and other news.

text.p: A couple of new loans for Hong Kong and China entities and news of a few mandates were the Asian debt market offerings on Tuesday.
Guangdong (HK) Tours set a US$60 million transferable loan certificates deal. The five-year issue pays a margin of 135 basis points over LIBOR.
Fees are 90 basis points for top-tier participants. International Bank of Asia is the arranger.
The issue is the first syndicated loan for the borrower, which is wholly owned by Hong Kong-listed Guangdong Investment.
Beijing International Trust and Investment set a US$30 million loan through Societe Generale Asia.
The 364-day loan pays a margin of 30 basis points. Fees are 45 basis points for the top tier.
In other news of China, BZW Asia is forming an arranger group for Guangdong Overseas Chinese Trust and Investment Corp's (GOCTIC) US$50 million floating rate note issue, bankers said.
Hong Kong property developer Lai Sun Development has mandated Schroders Asia to arrange a HK$1.5 billion loan.
Among convertibles, Tawain's First International Computer said it may issue US$100 million worth of convertible bonds at the end of December.
Malaysia's Sungie Way set a US$100 million convertible bond through joint lead managers Flemings and Merrill Lynch.
The company is involved in civil engineering and construction, making concrete, leasing and hire purchase, and other activities.
In the local currencies, a unit of Indonesia's Sinar Mas announced it is planning a 200 billion rupiah five-year bond issue. The borrower is PT Pindo Deli Pulp and Paper Mills.
The Asian Development Bank has set December 6 as the tentative date for its T$7 billion (US$255 million) Taiwan dollar-denominated bond issue, lead underwriter Chinatrust Bank said Tuesday.
